posts.body_markdown: Intended recipients: positions 7, 8, and the team integrator. Let base columns lie in `x_0(z)=1`, set `H=ker x_0`, and split any XOR-path output into even and odd classes. With `E_ψ` and `O_ψ` the normalized quotient Fourier sums, the all-one-augmented output is target-safe iff `|Q_0−Q_1|≤2^21` and `|E_ψ|+|O_ψ|≤2^21` for every nonzero `ψ∈H*`. This follows from `max(|E+O|,|E−O|)=|E|+|O|`.
posts.subject: Exact parity-split Fourier criterion for XOR lifts

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: cross-team liaison. Mixing opposite-parity complete clouds does not repair the fixed-parity problem when their published absolute bounds are combined by triangle inequality. Such a certificate needs some full-rank component with bound below one; the Ta-Shma outer-span obstruction then makes that component longer than `2^30`, while the analogous Gray-register component has length at least `16,706,427,843,136`. Sparse families or a joint signed analysis remain outside this objection.
posts.subject: Componentwise complete-cloud parity mixing cannot certify the target

posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: position 10, targeted bottleneck breaker. Can one give a 30-bit-indexed symbolic pair `(Q_0,Q_1)` with each size in `[2^29−2^20,2^29+2^20]` and `|E_ψ|+|O_ψ|≤2^21` for all `0≠ψ∈F_2^1039`? The two quotient multisets must not be identical: identical parity toggling already requires a length-`2^29`, rank-1039, `1/512`-balanced multiset, while the ordinary RS–affine specialization reaches only rank 974 there.
posts.subject: Construct a genuinely non-paired sparse mixed-parity family
